sources.title: MIT · Pavel Etingof：Lie Groups and Lie Algebras
sources.note: Lie group , mathematical background for representation, coverage and root systems. Class examples, text, and illustrations are written independently, and handout titles or pages are not copied.

sources.title: University of Alberta · Vincent Bouchard：Unitary representations
sources.note: conjugate transpose , unitary matrix and the basic definitions of complex inner products.

sources.title: University of Alberta · Vincent Bouchard：SU(2)
sources.note: SU(2) generator and its two-to-one mapping to SO(3); this class uniformly adopts the symbol convention of U=exp(−iθT).

sources.title: MIT 8.323 · Wentao Cui: Recitation 7, part SU(2)
sources.note: Spin labels and dimensions of SU(2) irreducible representations. Only the SU(2) section is cited; local Lie-algebra relations are not equated with global representations of arbitrary groups.

sources.title: University of Cambridge · David Tong：The Standard Model，The Strong Force
sources.note: checks against standard Gell-Mann matrix, Tₐ=λₐ/2, trace normalization and Cartan generator . The three-level demonstration does not simulate QCD.

sources.title: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory：Symmetry in Rotation
sources.note: Teaching background of half-integer spin rotation and neutron interference; the class clearly distinguishes the overall phase and the relative phase of the two paths.

sources.title: Walther-Meißner-Institut · Control of quantum two-level systems
sources.note: Coherent driving, detuning and Rabi oscillation in a rotating coordinate system; this class uses self-defined Ω, Δ and initial |↑⟩, and does not directly apply the ground state symbols in the lecture notes.

sources.title: UC Berkeley · Budker Group：Rabi Tutorial
sources.note: Periodically driven two-level systems; used to check the physics background, and independent analytical derivation of the constant effective Hamiltonian is used in class.

sources.title: MIT 8.05 · Barton Zwiebach：Addition of Angular Momentum
sources.note: angular momentum coupling with spin–orbit coupling background. Numerical examples and exercises for the class are written independently.

sources.title: University of Cambridge · Hugh Osborn：Group Theory Lecture Notes
sources.note: Sections 3.6–3.7 give SU(2) tensor products and Clebsch–Gordan conventions; Sections 7.3–7.6 cover SU(3) representations and tensor products. The Casimir normalization in Section 7.3.3 differs from this course; convert to Tₐ=λₐ/2 before comparing.

sources.title: Alex, Kalus, Huckleberry, von Delft: SU(N) Clebsch–Gordan Numerical Algorithm
sources.note: J. Math. Phys. 52, 023507 (2011), doi:10.1063/1.3521562. Used to check the concepts of GT, highest weight and multiplicity ; the paper proposes numerical algorithms, and this class also writes limited range numerical and precise algebra implementations. Phase and copy base selection are not guaranteed to be the same item by item.

sources.title: LMU Munich · SU(N) Clebsch–Gordan generator：Conventions
sources.note: The GT pattern, status label, and outer multiplicity indicator publicly described by the author. The classroom uses this to distinguish representation labels, state labels, and copy labels of the same type; the remote calculator is not called.

sources.title: SymPy Official documentation: Best Practices · Exact Rational Numbers vs. Floats
sources.note: Check the difference between rational numbers, radicals and floating point input. This class accurately implements the GT construct independently; safe expression input uses restricted syntax and does not hand over any string to Python for execution.

sources.title: Dang, Draayer, Pan, Becker: U(3) coupling and recoupling coefficients
sources.note: EPJ Plus 139, 704 (2024), doi:10.1140/epjp/s13360-024-05501-8. Preprint V.1, equations (27)–(28) give the U coefficient of triple coupling path with outer multiplicity index; IV.3–IV.4 illustrate highest weight and phase transfer. This class's triple Racah experiment implements two adjacent brackets of the common SU(3), using its own GT convention.

sources.title: Lanina, Sleptsov: Racah matrix with 6j normalization
sources.note: Physics Letters B 845, 138138 (2023), Section 2.1, Eqs. (2.4)–(2.5). Used to check multiplicity-space maps and normalization by the square root of the two intermediate-representation dimensions. This course takes the ordinary-group q→1 limit and ordinary dimensions; quantum groups and braid groups are not calculated.

sources.title: Dang, Draayer, Pan, Becker: Four recoupling and 9-U(3) recoupling coefficients
sources.note: V.2. Equation (30) gives the unitary 9-U(3) coefficient between the two pairing trees, which can be obtained through the 6-U and 6-Z coefficients. This class is independently composed of CG embedding and taking the inner product, using R to represent the unitary overlap; the dimension reduction 9j table S is also defined instead of copying the equation (30) as it is into S. The GT phase, replica base and normalization of SU(3) are noted separately.

conventions: U(theta)=exp(-i theta T); Hermitian T=sigma/2 or lambda/2
UI parameters displayed in degrees; public Python API receives radians
dimension is fundamental representation dimension; realDimension is manifold dimension
SU(3) Cartan weight diagram is not a real-space crystal diagram
SU(2) CG coefficients use Condon-Shortley phases
Rabi frequencies are angular frequencies in a common chosen time unit; H_eff/hbar=(Omega sigma_x+Delta sigma_z)/2
SU(3) highest weights use Dynkin (p,q); exact integer weight multiplicities do not determine a CG basis
SU(3) CG matrix columns are coupled orthonormal GT states in the ordered product basis; b=C^dagger a and a=C b
Highest-weight phase and deterministic outer-multiplicity conventions are explicit; identical-factor copies resolve exchange parity
Exact CG coefficients are constructed over rational/radical arithmetic and verified before numerical approximations are generated
Racah F has right paths as rows and left paths as columns; b_R=F b_L; paths retain both binary vertex multiplicities
Dimension-reduced six-j S_fe=F_fe/sqrt(dimE dimF), in this GT gauge; S has dimension-weighted orthogonality
Four-factor R has right paired paths as rows and left paired paths as columns; right tensor order ACBD is explicitly returned to ABCD; b_R=R b_L
Dimension-reduced nine-j S=R/sqrt(dimE dimF dimG dimH), with dimension-weighted orthogonality; three outer copies per path
